note: Ana checks a train journey from the station to the museum area. The train leaves at nine in the morning and arrives at ten. She asks both questions, obtains her ticket, boards before departure, then gets off after arrival. A clearly separate return service is introduced only after this journey ends. Teach leaves/arrives in contextual statements and leave/arrive in exact does-question bindings. Do not assume generic does grammar is already known. Actual clocks, schedule, recordings and chronology must agree.

lesson.title: 6.12 What Time Does It Leave?
lesson.unit_outcome: Name places and transport, explain a current destination, complete a trip, follow directions, ask for help, choose a service and check its times.
lesson.goal: Ask for departure and arrival times, then use them in one achievable journey.
lesson.grammar_function: Ana checks a train journey from the station to the museum area. The train leaves at nine in the morning and arrives at ten. She asks both questions, obtains her ticket, boards before departure, then gets off after arrival. A clearly separate return service is introduced only after this journey ends.
lesson.prerequisite: Units 1–5 and the earlier Unit 6 lessons in the displayed course sequence.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Ask for departure and arrival times, then use them in one achievable journey.
